questions.questionText: In a triangle, two angles are 60° and 70°. Find the third angle.
questions.explanation: Sum of angles in triangle = 180°. Third angle = 180° − 60° − 70° = 50°.

questions.questionText: Two angles are on a straight line. If one angle is 75°, what is the other?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°. Other = 180° − 75° = 105°.

questions.questionText: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. The opposite angle = 65°.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one angle is 50°, what is the corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal. The corresponding angle = 50°.

questions.questionText: Find the sum of interior angles of a hexagon (6 sides).
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°. For hexagon: (6 − 2) × 180° = 4 × 180° = 720°.

questions.questionText: A right triangle has legs 3 cm and 4 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: Pythagoras: c² = a² + b² = 9 + 16 = 25. c = 5 cm.

questions.questionText: An isosceles triangle has a base of 10 cm and equal sides of 13 cm. Find the height.
questions.explanation: Half base = 5. Pythagoras: h² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144. h = 12 cm.

questions.questionText: Find the area of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of parallelogram = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.questionText: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of trapezium = ½ × (a + b) × h = ½ × (6 + 10) × 4 = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².

questions.questionText: Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 14 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 10 × 14 = 70 cm².

questions.questionText: Find the perimeter of a rectangle with length 12 cm and width 5 cm.
Find the area of a rectangle with length 8 cm and width 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle = length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.questionText: A square has a side of 9 cm. Find its perimeter.
A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm, and 9 cm. Find its perimeter.

questions.questionText: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.

questions.questionText: Find the volume of a cuboid with length 5 cm, width 4 cm, and height 3 cm.
questions.explanation: Volume of cuboid = length × width × height = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³.

questions.explanation: Modal class = class with highest frequency = 30-40 (frequency 12).

questions.questionText: Frequency table: Class 5-10 has freq 3, 10-15 has freq 7, 15-20 has freq 10, 20-25 has freq 5. What is the modal class?
questions.explanation: Modal class = class with highest frequency = 15-20 (frequency 10).

questions.questionText: Find the cumulative frequency up to class 20-30, given: class 0-10 has freq 3, 10-20 has freq 5, 20-30 has freq 8.
questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency = sum of frequencies up to and including the class. 3 + 5 + 8 = 16.

questions.questionText: A trader bought 25 books at RM 18 each and sold them all at RM 24 each. What is the total profit?

questions.questionText: A car travels 60 km at 30 km/h, then another 60 km at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Time1 = 60/30 = 2h. Time2 = 60/60 = 1h. Total distance = 120 km, total time = 3h. Average = 120/3 = 40 km/h.

questions.explanation: Let Bala = x. Ahmad = 3x. Total: x + 3x = 24. 4x = 24. x = 6. Ahmad = 3 × 6 = RM 18.

questions.questionText: A rope of 50 m is cut into 3 pieces. The second piece is twice the first, and the third piece is 10 m longer than the first. Find the length of the first piece.
questions.explanation: Let first = x. Second = 2x. Third = x + 10. Total: x + 2x + (x + 10) = 50. 4x + 10 = 50. 4x = 40. x = 10.

Find the 10th term of the sequence: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, …
questions.explanation: Arithmetic sequence: first term a = 3, common difference d = 4. nth = a + (n−1)d. 10th = 3 + 9(4) = 39.

questions.questionText: Find the 5th term of the geometric sequence: 2, 6, 18, 54, …
questions.explanation: Geometric sequence: first term = 2, common ratio = 3. 5th term = 2 × 3^4 = 2 × 81 = 162.

questions.questionText: Simplify: a⁰ × b³ (where a ≠ 0) = ?

questions.explanation: Change = 22 − 40 = −18 litres. Time = 3 hours. Rate = −18/3 = −6 litres/hour. Magnitude = 6 litres/hour.

questions.questionText: Find the x-intercept of the line 2x − 3y = 6.

questions.explanation: Parallel lines have same gradient. y = 3x − 5 has gradient 3 (parallel).

questions.explanation: Total cost = 5(4) + 3(6) = 20 + 18 = RM 38. Total mass = 8 kg. Price = 38/8 = RM 4.75.

An inscribed angle in a circle subtends an arc of 60°. What is the inscribed angle?
questions.explanation: Inscribed angle theorem: inscribed angle = ½ × arc. So ½ × 60° = 30°.

questions.questionText: In a circle of radius 13 cm, a chord is 10 cm long. Find the perpendicular distance from the centre to the chord.

questions.questionText: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 17 cm and a base of 16 cm. Find its height (from apex perpendicular to base).

questions.explanation: y × x = constant = 12 × 8 = 96. When x = 16: y = 96/16 = 6 days.

questions.questionText: Find the equation of a line with slope 3 passing through (0, 4).
questions.explanation: Slope-intercept form: y = mx + c. m = 3, y-intercept c = 4. So y = 3x + 4.

questions.questionText: On a distance-time graph, a horizontal line segment means the object is:
questions.explanation: Horizontal line = distance doesn't change = object is stopped.

questions.questionText: Line 1: y = 2x + 1. Line 2: slope is −1/2. Are these perpendicular?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to −1. 2 × (−1/2) = −1. Yes, perpendicular.
